AdminUsers.dc.html.title: Jail Admin 3: Users and auditor logins

n1.text:
What is confusing today

1. Sidebar is a flat list of 10 groups with no icons; 'Search' appears under Facilities, Residents, Rules, Funds and Cash Drawers, so the same word means five things.
2. No home page: login lands on Release Notes.
3. Facility page is one 7-screen scroll: address, limits, taxes, debit cards, schedules, locations, class codes, products and packs all stacked.
4. Resident page shows balance but no visible way to deposit, withdraw or adjust.
5. Icon-only actions (eye, pencil, print, sliders) with no labels or tooltips.
6. Resident table overflows sideways even at 1536px.
7. Products, Packs, Attributes, Categories, Tags and Class Codes are six separate top-level pages.

n2.text:
Design moves

- Group nav by job: Operate (Residents, Orders, Finances), Catalog (Products and sub-areas), Setup (Facilities, Rules, Admins, Warehouses).
- Global search bar in the header finds a resident, facility, item or order from anywhere.
- Facility selector in the header filters every list.
- Primary actions are labeled buttons, not icons.
- Long settings pages become section tabs with a sticky jump list.
- Status is shown as colored chips, not Yes/No text.

n6.text:
Prodigy Admin view rules

- Prodigy staff see every facility. A facility selector in the header scopes the page; 'All facilities' shows the fleet.
- From any facility, Prodigy can open that jail's Officer, Manager, Jail Admin or Auditor view ('View as') to support them, with the session logged as Prodigy.
- Prodigy-only setup lives here: JMS feed, card processor, kiosks, warehouses, products and pricing, tax groups, scheduled tasks, batches.
- Accounting keeps the full ledger, commissions and bank accounts across facilities.
- The first-row drafts (Main, Resident, Facility) were the first pass; this row supersedes them.

n5.text:
Auditor view rules (from the roles plan)

- Read-only, time-limited login covering one or more facilities. Created by the Jail Administrator or Prodigy Support.
- One report library page grouped by the audit test each report supports. Facility and date range picked once at the top.
- Every report prints to PDF and emails from the same button, with facility, period, run date and who ran it in the footer.
- Reports map to what Oklahoma SAI and Texas county auditors actually test: receipts to deposits, sequential receipts and voids, bank-to-books reconciliation, releases against signed forms, disbursements by purpose, commissary transfers, segregation of duties, stale checks.
- Every report run is logged.

n4.text:
Manager view rules (from the roles plan)

- Home page is the daily close-out checklist: count drawer, bank deposit, releases, orders, then reconcile monthly.
- The county holds the trust fund bank account, so the bank deposit step documents the deposit and prints the slip; it does not move money.
- Drawer count records who counted and who verified. Over/Short needs a note.
- Releases pay out only after the release form is marked signed.
- Commissary transfer shows the running amount due and the sales report behind it.
- Each audit test from the Craig County OK and Burnet County TX reports maps to a step here.

n3.text:
Officer view rules (from the roles plan)

- One facility, fixed in the header. No facility picker.
- Four jobs on the home page: Find inmate, New inmate, Deposit, Bill inmate.
- Deposit asks one question: what was received? Cash, check or money order, card. No ledger accounts, no source or destination medium.
- Check holds: no default length, officer sets it, Manager can release early.
- Every money transaction has a Fix button; options depend on type. Fixes post a reversing entry and print a corrected receipt.
- Approval thresholds are off unless the Jail Administrator turns them on.
